description: Conversion of house into 2 flats including single-storey rear extension and loft extension
decision_conditions: Reason : 1 - The proposal by reason of size would fail to provide an acceptable standard of residential accommodation in a cramped and unsatisfactory standard of accommodation to the detriment of the amenities of future occupiers for future occupiers of Flat A. The proposal would therefore be contrary to policies London Plan 2021 policy D6, H11.1 and D12.3 of the Merton Local Plan 2024 and the Technical Housing Standards - Nationally Described Space Standard.

Reason : 2 - In the absence of detailing of the front boundary treatment, the scheme would increase visual permeability into a predominately hard surfaced forecourt which fails to positively contribute to the visual amenity of the streetscene contrary to, in particular, D12.3 of the Merton Local Plan 2024

Reason : 3 - The development has failed to provide sufficient secure, integrated, convenient and accessible cycle parking facilities, contrary to policies T16.1 and T16.2 of Merton's Local Plan 2024 and T5 of the London Plan 2021.

Reason : 4 - In the absence of adequate refuse and recycling storage facilities for the development, in particular, Flat A, the applicant has not demonstrated that the scheme would safeguard the free flow of traffic in the locality to the detriment of highway and pedestrian safety and safeguard the visual amenity� of the area.� The scheme is contrary to, in particular, Policies D3, D4, D6, T4, T7, SI 7 & SI 8 of the London Plan 2021, Merton Local Plan 2024 policy D12.2, D12.3, W14.4, T16.1, T16.3 and T16.4.

Reason : 5 - In the absence of a completed S106 undertaking to ensure that new dwellings are prevented from being able to obtain parking permits for the Controlled Parking Zone, the proposal would result in an increased demand for on street parking, resulting in a detrimental impact on highway and additional parking pressure locally and be contrary to the Mayor and the Council's commitment to reducing car usage and promoting more sustainable forms of transport. The proposal would therefore be contrary to policy T4, T6 of the London Plan 2021, policies T16.1, T16.3 and T16.4 of the Merton Local Plan 2024

Reason : 6 -  By reason of the absence of an energy statement (demonstrating that the scheme would achieve a 100% improvement on Part L, Building regulations 2021), absence of information to demonstrate water usage rates and absence of information relating to ventilation or overheating, the applicant has failed to demonstrate compliance with, in particular, Policies CC2.1, CC2.2, CC2.3, CC2.4 CC2.5 and CC2.6 of the Merton Local Plan 2024 and London Plan policies SI2 and SI4..

Reason : 7 - In the absence of a legal agreement to secure an appropriate contribution towards offsite affordable housing or a satisfactory financial viability assessment to justify the lack of, the scheme fails to address the recognised housing need and will be contrary to, in particular, Policy H11.1 of Merton's Local Plan 2024.

Reason : 8 - In the absence of a Flood Risk Assessment incorporating Sustainable Urban Drainage Design, it has not been demonstrated the scheme would safeguard the risk of flooding in the locality.  The proposal is contrary to, in particular, London Plan 2021 policy SI 13, Merton Local Plan 2024 policies F15.8 and F15.9

Reason : 9 - In the absence of a satisfactory Air Quality Neutral Statement, the applicant has failed to demonstrate that the development would be at minimum air quality neutral, not worsening local air quality thereby failing to comply with policy SI1 of the London Plan 2021

Reason : 10 - INFORMATIVE
Note to Applicant
In accordance with paragraph 38 of the NPPF, The London Borough of Merton  (LBM) takes a positive and proactive approach to development proposals focused on solutions. LBM works with applicants/agents in a positive and proactive manner by:
"	Offering a pre-application advice and duty desk service. 
"	Where possible, suggesting solutions to secure a successful outcome.
"	As appropriate, updating applicants/agents of any issues that may arise in the processing of their application.
In this instance:
"	The application was not considered to comply with the provisions of the Development Plan and NPPF as submitted, and would have required substantial changes such that a new application would be required. 
"	The application was considered to be fundamentally contrary to the provisions of the Development Plan and the NPPF, and there were not considered to be any solutions to resolve this conflict. 
"	It is noted that the applicant/agent did not engage in any pre-application discussions.
"	The applicant is advised to seek pre-application advice on any resubmission.
